📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Once America’s most popular electric pickup, the Ford F-150 Lightning is finding a second life on the used market.

The F-150 Lightning is hard to pass up at 50% to 60% off sticker price, even used. With latest models no longer available, Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes on the used market.

After the last model rolled off the assembly line last December, CEO Jim Farley noted the decision to end production came as the “very high-end EVs, the $50K, 70K, $80,000 vehicles, they just weren’t selling.”.

Recent findings suggest that at 50% to 60% off, it now looks like a bargain in the used market. “When Ford was selling it brand upcoming, the math was complicated,” Jimmy Douglas, CEO of Plug, a wholesale EV dealer, recently told Bloomberg.

On the used market, however, “the Lightning is 50% to 60% of the sticker price and that is really a sweet spot,” he added.

Sources indicate that used Ford F-150 Lightnings are selling in about 20 days, less than half the 44-day average for used vehicles in the US. According to Edmunds.com, prices are now up 4% to about $50,000 since the start of the year.

Douglass noted that close to one-third of used models are sold by rival dealerships that would normally flip them back to Ford. However, many are opting to sell them directly because of demand.

Chase Norris from Colorado called the electric pickup a bargain. He purchased a used Lightning for around $40,000 and considers it a major upgrade from his previous gas F-150.

EV Group CEO and cofounder Alex Lawrence, which sells pre-owned electric vehicles, said he can’t get his hands on any reasonably priced used F-150 Lightnings currently.

He noted many Lightning buyers use it as a second truck to save money during their weekly commute.

It looks essentially the same as the gas-powered F-150, offers instant torque, and produces zero tailpipe emissions, but the electric pickup failed to meet Ford’s expectations because of its higher price.

The base F-150 Lightning Pro debuted in 2021 with a starting MSRP of $39,974, but that was promptly raised to around $60,000 a year or so later.

Recent findings suggest that according to Edmunds.com, the average transaction price for the F-150 Lightning in its first year of sales was $79,000 because Ford focused on higher-priced trims. The gas version’s ATP was about $19,000 less.

Industry observers note that even with the higher sticker price, Ford was losing a considerable amount on each Lightning it produced. In Q1 2024, Ford lost more than $100,000 on every EV it built.

Next year, Ford will take another crack at the electric pickup market with the Fathom, the first vehicle based on its “groundbreaking” new Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform.

According to recent reports, ford remarked the Fathom will start at $28,350 for the standard-range version. Even with the $1,595 delivery fee included, the electric pickup will start at under $30,000.

As the first vehicle built on its UEV platform, Ford promises the Fathom will be a step-change from its first-generation EVs.

According to Ford, the electric pickup will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4 and will be the first vehicle with Apple Maps directly integrated into the navigation system.

We also know the electric pickup will have a NACS port after a few prototypes were spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger this summer.

Ford reportedly aims to sell around 100,000 Fathoms in its first year. CEO Jim Farley said on the tech giant’s third-quarter earnings call last week that the launch remains on track for Q4 2027.

Farley called the Fathom a “breakthrough product” and remarked that the MSRP under $30,000 is perfect for today’s market.

At least some F-150 owners are already trading in for lower-priced options. A member of the Ford F-150 Lightning Owners Group, JF, noted that although it was a great ride, “Carvana gave us just a little less than we paid latest,” adding, “R2, here we come!”.

When Torque News reached out, JF said he “really liked the Lightning,” but wanted something smaller. “With the current increase in resale value, the time to trade seemed right,” JF added.

It has been revealed that the Rivian R2 (see our review) Performance with the Launch Package is now available to order starting at $57,990 with an EPA-estimated range of up to 330 miles and 656 hp. The R2 Premium will go on sale later this year, starting at $53,990.

In Spring 2027, Rivian will launch the R2 Standard, starting at $44,990 with an estimated range of up to 275 miles and 350 hp.

So were they losing $100k / truck, or the average loss when all development was included ended up being $100k? Significant difference. I don't believe the cost to build each one was $170k+. That makes no sense. They just priced them too high to amortize the development costs over enough vehicles to make them profitable. Every vehicle has to sell a minimum # before they start to make a profit.

Surging F-150 Lightning sales on the used market show buyers want electric pickups. But at the right price.

Sources indicate that at $60,000 to $70,000, the Lightning wasn’t so attractive, but at $40,000 used, it suddenly is. Perhaps Ford is on to something with its next-gen EV pickup, the Fathom, set to go on sale starting at under $30,000.

Recent findings suggest that will it deliver on its promise? Ford has yet to reveal battery specs, towing capacity, range, or any other specs. We should learn more soon.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on Nov. 16, and the proposal lowers the maximum annual issuance of NEAR Protocol from 2.5% to 1.6%. On Tuesday, the price of NEAR dipped to $3.12 in the morning and then went back up to $3.26.

HSP-029 was written by Sal Ternullo, CEO of SVRN, and opened for forum discussion on Oct. 7. The vote closed on Nov. 2, and 99.96% of the veNEAR cast was in favor of the proposal; no veNEAR was cast against it. The Security Council's 14-day window to veto the proposal closed on Nov. 16 with no veto, according to House of Stake.

In a recent development, this is the second inflation cut for NEAR in just over a year. In October 2025, the maximum issuance was halved from the original 5% to 2.5%, and in September 2026, the realized issuance stood at 2.45%, according to HSP-029.

At 1.6%, NEAR will have "one of the lowest annual issuance rates among major blockchains," House of Stake stated.

Sources indicate that according to House of Stake, the reduction will start one quarter after ratification, and validators still have to adopt the protocol upgrade. The issuance cap will reach 1.6% after 24 months.

Ternullo estimated in HSP-029 that NEAR will avoid issuing 11.8 million tokens over two years. At the current price, these tokens would be worth around $38.5 million.

The proposal also calculated that the staking yield of NEAR will go down from around 5.27% to around 3.37% if the staking ratio stays the same. More than half of all NEAR is not staked, according to House of Stake.

According to recent reports, bitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes recently named NEAR among four tokens that he expects to rise before the end of the AI bubble. Hayes set targets of $6 for NEAR, $2,800 for ETH, $1,800 for ZEC, and $40 for VVV.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Google DeepMind researchers say their AI agents produced mathematical proofs linking specific security guarantees to a compiled build of Signal’s encryption library, and they put the resulting evidence online for others to check.
  • 10 AlphaProof Code report describes about 6.5 million lines of machine-checked Lean proof code.
  • Sources indicate that the authors say five people worked on the proofs over four weeks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google DeepMind researchers say their AI agents produced mathematical proofs linking specific security guarantees to a compiled build of Signal’s encryption library, and they put the resulting evidence online for others to check.

The Nov. 10 AlphaProof Code report describes about 6.5 million lines of machine-checked Lean proof code. The result concerns a particular build of libsignal, the Signal protocol’s implementation, under explicit assumptions about cryptography and the environment in which the code runs.

Sources indicate that the authors say five people worked on the proofs over four weeks. Humans directed the work, selected reference models and reviewed the specifications that defined what the agents had to prove.

The target was an AArch64 Linux executable using libsignal-protocol v0.105.4 and SPQR v1.6.0 inside a small command-line harness. The theorems cover session initialization, sending a message, and receiving one. Key generation falls outside that verified scope.

The Google report connects the compiled executable to specified properties of PQXDH and Triple Ratchet one-to-one messaging, including forward secrecy, authentication, and post-compromise security.

These address whether earlier messages stay secret after keys are stolen, whether senders are authentic, and whether a session can regain secrecy after a compromise.

Its two proof models provide different assurances: the symbolic analysis relies on idealized cryptographic operations and collision-free executions, while the computational analysis bounds the success of classical attackers under stated cryptographic assumptions.

DeepMind’s reported process connects human-selected requirements and one executable to a machine-checked proof, with trusted assumptions still defining the result.

A checked proof establishes the stated guarantee for the specified build and model.

Author-reported proofs for a specific AArch64 Linux harness. Specifications, execution model, routine contracts and cryptographic assumptions remain trusted. No direct verification of phone apps, key generation or groups; no independent rebuild performed here.

Source-bound schematic of the reported proof workflow and trust boundary; connectors show logical dependence, not elapsed time or measured security strength.

It has been revealed that author-reported proofs for a specific AArch64 Linux harness. Specifications, execution model, routine contracts and cryptographic assumptions remain trusted. No direct verification of phone apps, key generation or groups; no independent rebuild performed here.

The symbolic proof establishes handshake secrecy under specified later breaks of Diffie-Hellman, but the computational proof does not cover quantum attackers. Group messaging is outside the report’s scope, and the computational model excludes multi-device state. Its bounds also stop providing a useful guarantee at sufficiently large workloads.

The results still require trust in Lean’s checking kernel, the specifications reviewed by the researchers, the AArch64 Linux model, and contracts describing selected routines.

In a recent development, the project’s Nov. 11 update, merged on GitHub, claims ten more library routines were verified, cutting trusted routine hooks from 37 to 27. Those hooks replace execution of selected routines with assumed descriptions of their behavior.

In a recent development, the update retains libsignal v0.105.4 but changes the pinned executable. The newer build verifies the machine code for those ten routines instead of relying on their modeled contracts.

It has been revealed that the project repository provides public instructions to rebuild the pinned binary and check its proofs. A Linux-only comparator checks that the theorems and their dependent definitions match trusted statements, then replays proofs in a fresh Lean kernel.

According to recent reports, the authors also report reintroducing two previously fixed libsignal bugs and proving that the modified binaries violate their symbolic security theorem. That tests whether the specification rejects those known regressions.

The public package gives other researchers a concrete way to check the claimed connection between security requirements and executable code.

Ledger, a crypto wallet firm, said it had experienced a security incident related to Optimizely, a third-party service used on its official website, but reassured its owners about the security of their devices and private keys.

In a post, Ledger remarked it was aware of a security incident impacting Optimizely, a third-party service provider used by many other sites as well.

In a recent development, we are aware of a security incident affecting Optimizely, a third-party service used on https://t.co/d2pWxdG49X, alongside numerous other websites. Our team has remediated the issue, and the malicious code is no longer being served through our website. This incident does not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices. Your private keys remain protected by your Ledger device. For more information from Optimizely: https://t.co/CxzmBxYadb.

Industry observers note that website optimization platform Optimizely said it had discovered and contained a security incident affecting some of its Web Experimentation customers on November 16, 2026. Optimizely stated that the vulnerable path has now been blocked, the injected code has been removed, and customers have been contacted directly.

Along these lines, Ledger confirmed that its team had remediated the issue and that the malicious code was no longer being served through its website.

Ledger emphasizes that the incident did not affect the security architecture of Ledger devices and that user private keys remain protected by their Ledger device, thus reassuring users that the incident had not compromised the core security of its wallet products.

According to researcher Scott Helme, on November 16, 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organizations' websites across several sectors through the Optimizely Web Experimentation platform. The websites included Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger, and Peacock.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed, with only 1 of the 188 infected snippets found, down from 169.

The main point is that trusted JavaScript is not always trustworthy. A third-party dependency can exploit a website without ever breaking the website's own code or infrastructure.

Latest Update: Janus Electric secures battery supply deal for its battery-swap semi truck

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that australian conversion specialists Janus Electric have been celebrating a growing slate of orders for their Class 8 electric truck conversions, which ditch diesel in favor of advanced battery-swap electric power – but exactly how they’d deliver all those trucks was still a question.
  • The concept of dropping an electric power unit into a Class 8 semi makes perfect sense, as most of these trucks are built as gliders.
  • Janus’ reservation book crept past 70 units this past summer, helped along in part by California’s HVIP Program and the US EPA’s Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) Grants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that australian conversion specialists Janus Electric have been celebrating a growing slate of orders for their Class 8 electric truck conversions, which ditch diesel in favor of advanced battery-swap electric power – but exactly how they’d deliver all those trucks was still a question. Now, we have an answer: Electrovaya will supply the batteries.

The concept of dropping an electric power unit into a Class 8 semi makes perfect sense, as most of these trucks are built as gliders. That is, rolling body and chassis without an engine and transmission that’s ready to receive power from Cummins, Detroit, International, or Volvo Penta. That’s the role that Janus Electric sees itself occupying, and it seems to be working.

Janus’ reservation book crept past 70 units this past summer, helped along in part by California’s HVIP Program and the US EPA’s Diesel Emission Reduction Act (DERA) Grants. When the HVIP voucher is combined with the Port of Los Angeles’ “Plus” support, customers can received up to $166,000 per truck conversion. Factor in the massive fuel savings of electric and the classic good looks of square-nose Western Star truck body, and it’s easy to see why they’d be a popular choice.

In a recent development, as Jerry Seinfeld taught us however, it’s one thing to take a reservation – it’s another thing to deliver. To help make it happen, Janus has inked a battery supply deal with Electrovaya that will see a $26 million initial purchase orders for Electrovaya battery packs to demand for Janus’ products in the US and Canada, along with the battery manufacturer purchasing approximately $1.4 million in Janus stock with (what seems to be) actual money.

“Electrovaya is an vital partner to Janus Electric, and we’re particularly pleased it has decided to invest directly in our business,” explains Ben Hutt, Managing Director and CEO of Janus Electric. “The investment is a strong vote of confidence in our technology and approach to electrifying heavy transport.”.

Industry observers note that the Janus Electric-repowered trucks carry a stout, 480 hp electric motor drawing power from a standard 310 kWh battery pack, with up to two battery packs (one on each side) of the truck. In practice, that gives the Janus trucks up to 370 miles of loaded range. After that, the batteries can be DC fast charged in under 90 minutes, or swapped for fresh ones in about four minutes without too much in the way of specialized equipment. That’s not just Janus’ killer app, it means that a battery supply deal like this one with a strategic partner who’s invested in the fledgling company’s success is such a huge deal.

“Reliable battery supply is critical to our growth,” adds Hutt, “and Electrovaya’s expanding North American manufacturing capabilities will be important as we scale. Both companies see considerable opportunity in this market, and we look forward to building on our partnership.”.

Industry observers note that for their part, Electrovoya executives seem to know their role here, and seem excited to be a part of what Janus is doing. “Class 8 trucking is one of the most exciting and demanding frontiers in electrification, and Janus has demonstrated real commercial traction with fleets in the US, Canada and Australia,” said Dr. Raj Das Gupta, CEO of Electrovaya. “Janus has developed a practical solution to one of the major challenges facing heavy transport, enabling diesel-powered trucks to be converted to electric without compromising their commercial operations.”.

Electrovaya will be expanding its American manufacturing capacity with lithium-ion cell, module, and battery pack production at its upcoming, potentially BABA-compliant facility in Jamestown, New York, which is expected to come online in 2027.

Home » Exchanges » Gate Adds GBP and EUR Banking Support for Gate Money via OpenPayd.

The expanded integration adds virtual pound accounts and euro SEPA rails across Gate’s unified financial platform.

Cryptocurrency and financial services platform Gate has expanded its multi-year partnership with financial infrastructure provider OpenPayd to support the international rollout of Gate Money, its unified fiat, crypto, and equities account.

Under the expanded agreement, Gate is integrating OpenPayd’s British pound (GBP) account infrastructure and euro (EUR) Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) payment rails across additional corporate entities.

The expansion builds on a partnership established in 2022, when Gate began using OpenPayd’s virtual IBANs to manage and reconcile European retail and corporate payment flows.

According to the companies, the additional GBP and EUR capabilities will support Gate Money while remaining available across Gate’s broader platform, which serves more than 62 million customers worldwide.

The infrastructure expansion follows the October 7, 2026 launch of Gate Money. The product brings digital assets, equities, payments and asset management together within a single account.

Consumers can hold, receive, transfer, pay and exchange GBP and EUR alongside digital assets, consolidating multiple financial activities within one platform.

The launch represents Gate’s expansion beyond cryptocurrency trading into broader financial services, with fiat payment infrastructure playing a central role in connecting traditional currencies and digital assets.

“Bringing assets, accounts and payments together requires fiat infrastructure that can operate across products and markets,” OpenPayd Chief Commercial Officer Lux Thiagarajah mentioned in a statement.

Recent findings suggest that gate Founder and CEO Dr. Han said the expanded partnership provides the financial infrastructure needed to integrate Gate’s services and simplify everyday fund management and payments for its global user base.

Gate’s expansion reflects a broader push by crypto exchanges to become all-in-one financial platforms.

Coinbase opened stock and ETF trading to all US consumers in February, while Kraken and Bybit have expanded into tokenized equities.

According to recent reports, gate announced a crypto-linked Visa card in early October, that is expected to reach more than 40 markets, allowing customers to spend their Gate Money balances at merchants. Its broader platform also provides access to metals, indices, forex and commodities, alongside more than 5,400 digital assets and 12,800 stocks and ETFs for trading.

For OpenPayd, the expanded agreement deepens its role in Gate’s financial services operations, strengthening its position as a provider connecting traditional banking with digital assets.

Founded in 2018, OpenPayd offers businesses a range of financial services through a single API, including embedded accounts, foreign exchange, domestic and international payments, Open Banking and stablecoin on- and off-ramps.

The organization says it serves more than 1,200 businesses, including eToro, Kraken, OKX and B2C2, and processes over $360 billion in annual transaction volumes.

For London-based OpenPayd, the expanded mandate adds to a growing roster of digital asset clients—including Kraken, OKX, Bybit, eToro, and B2C2—that rely on its API for fiat on/off-ramps and stablecoin settlement.

In a recent development, seamless fiat banking rails are the missing link for crypto exchanges trying to compete with traditional neobanks as everyday financial hubs. By wiring direct fiat infrastructure into their ecosystem, crypto platforms reduce reliance on third-party workarounds and make it easier for consumers to hold, convert, and spend traditional currencies alongside crypto and equities.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, bitcoin price barely reacted to widespread online banking and payment delays across major U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Crypto Market News » Bitcoin Holds $64K After US Bank Outages, but Demand Indicators Flash Warning.

Calm price action masks deeply negative on-chain demand and a shrinking profit cushion for Bitcoin holders.

In a recent development, bitcoin price barely reacted to widespread online banking and payment delays across major U.S. banks on Monday, though on-chain data suggests the price stability may mask underlying weakness in demand.

According to recent reports, bitcoin (BTC) edged down 0.2% over the past 24 hours to trade at $64,183 on Tuesday. Crypto market liquidations totaled $278.3 million over the same period—a moderate figure pointing to an absence of forced selling or panic. Bitcoin short liquidations accounted for $88.67 million, according to CoinGlass.

The muted market reaction came despite significant disruptions in traditional US banking infrastructure. According to the Associated Press, a software bug in JPMorgan Chase’s internal systems slowed transaction processing on Monday and triggered ripple effects across the wider banking network.

Customers at several major institutions, including Wells Fargo, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, Truist, and Capital One, reported delays, particularly when sending or receiving peer-to-peer transfers via Zelle involving Chase accounts.

While traditional payment rails faced bottlenecks and renewed scrutiny over centralized infrastructure, traders largely treated the incident as a temporary operational hiccup rather than a catalyst to rotate into crypto.

According to recent reports, beneath the calm surface, however, on-chain metrics point to persistent buyer hesitation. A report by CryptoQuant analyst MorenoDV highlights that Bitcoin’s “apparent demand” remains deeply negative.

On November 15, the 30-day reading was around -247,700 BTC, while the one-year figure stood at approximately -1.21 million BTC, with Bitcoin trading near $65,000.

The analyst notes the current contraction is among the sharpest negative readings in the period analyzed, with similar levels seen in March 2025 and mid-2026. However, he cautioned that the data does not mean Bitcoin is experiencing an unprecedented collapse or that its price has found a bottom.

What stands out more is how long the weakness has lasted. The 30-day reading has remained mostly negative throughout 2026, with only a brief recovery in late August.

Industry observers note that the one-year reading also turned negative around late May and has continued to decline. In other words, short-term improvements in demand have not lasted long enough to signal a sustained recovery.

Bitcoin’s earlier recovery toward $80,000–$85,000 did little to improve the longer-term demand trend. According to MorenoDV, this suggests the rebound lacked strong underlying demand.

It has been revealed that the analyst cautions that apparent demand is an indirect on-chain measure, not a direct record of BTC sales or capital outflows. Negative readings have also occurred during previous price recoveries, so the metric cannot reliably predict Bitcoin’s next move.

According to recent reports, for a stronger recovery signal, the 30-day reading would need to improve consistently, return above zero and eventually stabilize on the annual measure. Until then, persistent weak demand remains the main concern.

Another on-chain indicator reinforces the cautious outlook. Analyst Axel Adler Jr. reported that the share of Bitcoin supply in profit fell sharply to 52% (down 7% in a week), leaving the market close to an even split between coins held at a profit and those held at a loss.

Meanwhile, long-term holder (LTH) supply fell by 73,900 BTC to 16.2 million BTC, its lowest level in 90 days.

It has been revealed that according to Adler, both declines rank among the steepest of the past year, pointing to a shrinking profit cushion and faster redistribution of Bitcoin holdings. The market is now approaching a key threshold: below 50%, more than half of the circulating supply would be held at a loss.

A similar pattern emerged in August 2026, before Bitcoin rebounded by 24%. However, Adler cautions that one historical example is not enough to suggest the same recovery will happen again.

Bitcoin’s stability amid disruptions to traditional banking may suggest resilience, but the on-chain data tells a more cautious story. Persistent negative demand, a declining share of supply in profit and falling long-term holder balances point to weakening market support and a shrinking cushion against further price declines.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that XRP-paired trading on its native ledger nearly doubled over Nov. 9-15, but a separate comparison of the direct market for Ripple USD (RLUSD) at two dated ledgers highlighted a smaller execution penalty for a 100,000-XRP sale.

DefiLlama's daily data put completed Nov. 9-15 trading at $62.6 million, up 99.9% from $31.3 million during Nov. 2-8.

According to recent reports, the measure combines XRP-paired automated market maker swaps and order-book trades. Native XRP participates directly, but repeated turnover can recycle existing inventory without establishing fresh net buying.

In a recent development, NOSHASHI's ledger data showed the XRP/RLUSD automated market maker holding 2.165 million RLUSD at Nov. 9's close and 1.861 million on Nov. 16, a 14% decline. Native XRP in the same pool slipped from 1.972 million to 1.959 million.

Over that interval, sampled funded RLUSD offers available to token sellers increased from about 19,392 to 111,951 RLUSD, roughly 5.77 times the earlier amount. Funded amounts measure what the offer owners could deliver and may be below the advertised size.

NOSHASHI's measurement requests at most 100 offers per side and counts funded depth within 10% of each snapshot's reference midpoint. Its ask side is the RLUSD inventory an XRP seller receives, and the figures exclude AMM reserves, do not measure all XRP liquidity, and do not imply that every sampled offer sits near the best price.

Recent findings suggest that an idealized static model combined the Nov. 9 raw offers and pool state with their Nov. 16 equivalents. For each snapshot, it allocated XRP between funded offers and the constant-product pool according to which supplied more RLUSD for the next XRP sold.

Recent findings suggest that the pool calculation includes its ordinary trading fee, 0.308% at the earlier ledger and 0.315% at the later one. XRPL can combine offers and AMMs in an actual transaction, but this calculation is not account-specific pathfinding or a completed fill.

Recent findings suggest that the benchmark is the midpoint of the sampled book's tightest uncrossed bid and ask quotes, equivalent to about 1.098 RLUSD per XRP on Nov. 9 and 0.951 on Nov. 16.

In CryptoSlate's calculations, the shortfall for 100,000 XRP narrowed from 3.57% to 0.48% against each snapshot's own reference midpoint.

According to recent reports, this compares modeled proceeds with the token amount implied by that reference price and includes spread, modeled AMM fees, and price impact. The lower absolute proceeds on Nov. 16 reflect XRP's lower price in RLUSD, despite the smaller relative penalty.

The smaller trades did not share that improvement: the 1,000-XRP shortfall widened from 0.05% to 0.11%, while at 10,000 XRP, it widened from 0.05% to 0.19%.

It has been revealed that in the later snapshot, the larger modeled sale relied more heavily on funded offers. On Nov. 9, only about 17,701 XRP went to the sampled book, leaving 82,299 XRP for the pool. On Nov. 16, about 88,471 XRP went to offers and 11,529 XRP to the pool.

XRP-to-RLUSD execution shortfalls at two 2026 snapshots: November 9 close and November 16 at 13:07 UTC. The improvement depended on sale size.

Sources indicate that the earlier model assigned most XRP input to the pool. A higher reference price supported more RLUSD proceeds.

Industry observers note that the later model relied mainly on funded offers. The lower XRP price still meant fewer RLUSD received.

The modeled 100,000-XRP shortfall narrowed, but the same sale returned fewer RLUSD after XRP repriced.

Capped sample: 100 offers per side, within 10% of the reference mid. Assumes static liquidity and an eligible receiving trust line. Excludes deeper offers, other assets and additional transfer, network or redemption costs. Estimates are not pathfinding or completed fills; RLUSD is not bank cash.

Recent findings suggest that cryptoSlate static model combines funded offers and one constant-product AMM at ledgers 108227899 and 108367932. Shortfall = 100 × (1 − proceeds / (XRP sold / reference mid)); ordinary pool fees 0.308% and 0.315%. Bars share a zero-to-4% scale. Input-allocation strips total 100,000 XRP; values are rounded to whole XRP or RLUSD. Percentage labels and bar lengths use two decimal places.

Industry observers note that capped sample: 100 offers per side, within 10% of the reference mid. Assumes static liquidity and an eligible receiving trust line. Excludes deeper offers, other assets and additional transfer, network or redemption costs. Estimates are not pathfinding or completed fills; RLUSD is not bank cash.

These estimates exclude deeper offers, routes through other assets, additional issuer-transfer, network and redemption costs, and other account restrictions.

Swaps and liquidity-provider deposits or withdrawals can all change pool balances. A dollar-valued total value locked decline can also reflect repricing: DefiLlama's pool methodology excludes order-book offers and can double a pool's sole priced side, so its valuation buckets cannot establish literal token holdings or net deposits.

RLUSD proceeds also differ from dollars in a bank account. Ripple's user terms require Customer status under its customer agreement for direct issuer redemption, subject to applicable conditions.

The next useful evidence is whether funded offers persist and repeatable estimates remain favorable at the intended sale size.

This sample supports the conclusion that the larger direct RLUSD exit became less costly in the model even as the pool's RLUSD reserve shrank.

  • On the institutional front, JPMorgan has partnered with Singapore’s DBS Bank to launch a blockchain-based payment solution that allows institutional clients to transfer tokenized U.S dollar deposits between Singapore and the United States, 24/7.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two developments have caught the market’s attention.

Sources indicate that yi He, Co-CEO of Binance, revealed that her portfolio lost a total of $97.32 million over the last 30 days (17 October – 16 November). After adding in all transfers, this amounted to a total loss of $101.31 million. This, after Bitcoin lost over 16% of its value over the same timeframe — Its largest monthly loss in over four months.

On the institutional front, JPMorgan has partnered with Singapore’s DBS Bank to launch a blockchain-based payment solution that allows institutional clients to transfer tokenized U.S dollar deposits between Singapore and the United States, 24/7.

Together, these developments show two different sides of the market.

According to recent reports, on one hand, Yi He’s disclosure demonstrates just how deep the ongoing correction has been, with even major players taking a hit as selling pressure builds. On the other, JPMorgan’s partnership with DBS highlights that institutional interest in blockchain is still holding up despite the FUD and broader market weakness.

Recent findings suggest that this ties back to Yi He’s thesis that the ongoing pullback is only a short-term correction and there really isn’t any reason to panic. While prices continue to struggle, institutional activity suggests that long-term interest hasn’t disappeared.

Hence, the question is whether this conviction can eventually translate into a shift in sentiment.

Extreme fear has taken over the market.

According to the Bitcoin [BTC] Fear and Greed Index, sentiment levels fell to 10, indicating that the market was firmly in the “extreme fear” territory. The monthly average also seemed to be getting closer to this zone, with the same sitting at 28.2 at press time.

This suggests that fear is becoming more “persistent” rather than just a short-term reaction to market volatility. In fact, sentiment might soon be approaching levels last seen in February and June 2026, when Bitcoin faced deeper price declines.

And yet, Bitcoin’s Open Interest data showed that BTC was still accumulating new leveraged positions as it moved down from $83K to $74k. This may be evidence that while the market is becoming increasingly fearful, but it is yet to see leverage fully reset. This would leave BTC exposed to further volatility, especially if there isn’t fresh buying demand.

Against this backdrop, the significance of the two developments becomes clearer.

Extreme fear, Bitcoin’s 16% correction, and bearish on-chain signals could keep BTC under pressure in the near term. However, Yi He’s $97 million loss indicates not only the amount of stress on the market, but also that large institutions are continuing to increase/HODL their exposure to the blockchain space.

This might also mean that short-term market weakness has not necessarily changed the longer-term institutional outlook.

In this context, the 16% correction is more a general market correction rather than a loss of confidence in Bitcoin’s long-term potential.

Bitcoin’s 16% drop and high leverage point to further volatility.

JPMorgan’s partnership with DBS demonstrates that blockchain adoption is on the right track, despite the downturn.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Cryptopedia » 5 Tokens That Held Up Post-TGE.

While most crypto tokens struggle to maintain their launch valuations, these five projects have demonstrated varying degrees of post-TGE price resilience.

For almost all crypto tokens, the Token Generation Event (TGE) is the best day they will ever have.

For 2026, so far only about 28% of tokens debuted remained above their TGE closing price after 60 days. The median token was trading at just 0.64x its launch close.

Tokens surviving and rising in price for days, hours, and even minutes post-launch is not an easy feat. Here are five tokens that have so far avoided the typical post-TGE collapse:.

Today, $1WIN is trading around $0.045, roughly 50% above its public sale price.

In a recent development, it is too early to compare that performance with tokens that have been trading for months or years. What makes $1WIN worth paying attention to is that its held steady in the post-TGE price rise and has a significant business behind it. 1win has operated since 2016 with 100 million players and its gaming business is profitable independently of the token.

According to recent reports, the firm also plans revenue-funded open-market buybacks, while 10% of $1WIN spent through supported products will be burned. Supply is capped at one billion tokens with no additional minting.

Hyperliquid’s HYPE remains one of the clearest examples of a token that did considerably more than survive launch.

HYPE began trading in 2024 and today is hitting over $73, leaving it several multiples above its earliest market prices nearly two years later.

Sources indicate that the underlying exchange also gives the token an economic connection to platform activity. Trading fees flow into Hyperliquid’s Assistance Fund, which acquires HYPE, with accumulated tokens subsequently burned.

That combination of product usage, revenue and token demand makes HYPE one of the stronger examples of the kind of pre-TGE traction highlighted in Decasonic’s research.

Aster launched ASTER in September 2025 as the token behind its decentralized spot and perpetuals trading platform.

Sources indicate that despite substantial volatility since then, ASTER was trading around $0.65. It remains well below its $2.42 all-time high, but also far above its earliest trading levels.

ASTER has not gone up in a straight line. But more than a year after launch, the token has retained a substantial part of the value created during its early growth rather than fading toward zero after TGE.

Backpack’s BP demonstrates another type of post-TGE resilience.

Sources indicate that the token launched in March and subsequently fell as low as roughly $0.12 in May. By this month, BP had recovered to around $0.90, after reaching an all-time high of $1.66 in October.

In a recent development, that makes BP interesting because its strength did not come immediately after TGE. The token went through a deep early correction before rebuilding.

It also sits inside an established exchange and wallet ecosystem, with utility including trading-fee discounts, rewards, staking and access to other Backpack products.

ZAMA is trading around $0.067, approximately one-third above that public auction price.

The token also has direct utility within the Zama Protocol, where it is used to pay for encryption and decryption services and reward operators and stakers securing the network.

It has been revealed that stronger 2026 launches generally arrived with real usage, paying users, revenue, TVL or another measurable source of pre-TGE traction. The token was being added to something that already worked.

Hyperliquid had trading volume and fees. Backpack had its exchange and wallet. Zama had working privacy infrastructure. Aster had an operating trading platform. 1win entered TGE with a gaming business with 100 million players and has been operating since 2016.

A strong launch can be created by hype. Holding up once the launch is over usually requires much more.

  • The decision leaves a separate question for tokenized US stock markets about what protects investors when transaction ordering works against them.
  • The SEC had already opened a conditional route for those markets in September on its framework, which preserves applicable securities antifraud and manipulation laws, but requires venues to disclose their policies for MEV even when they have none.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A federal judge on Nov. 16 acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in a $25 million Ethereum maximum extractable value (MEV) exploit case because prosecutors had failed to prove a material misrepresentation.

The decision leaves a separate question for tokenized US stock markets about what protects investors when transaction ordering works against them.

The SEC had already opened a conditional route for those markets in September on its framework, which preserves applicable securities antifraud and manipulation laws, but requires venues to disclose their policies for MEV even when they have none.

MEV concerns the value captured through transaction ordering. Four operators' notices show how much can differ within that framework, from transaction privacy and planned sequencing controls to the prospect that investors bear their own losses.

Recent findings suggest that in her 46-page opinion, US District Judge Jessica Clarke found insufficient evidence to sustain wire fraud and the related wire-fraud and money-laundering conspiracy charges. The missing element was a material misrepresentation in the brothers' Omakase operation.

The opinion describes a 2023 operation that used lure transactions to attract sandwich-trading bots and exploited a relay-code vulnerability, producing about $25 million in 12 seconds. The targeted bots themselves sought to profit by placing transactions around someone else's trade, a practice that can leave that trader with a worse execution price.

The case was more specific than a simple claim that someone profited from transaction ordering, since prosecutors had to establish the charged fraud.

Clarke found that the trial evidence did not establish a material misrepresentation in the Omakase strategy, and frustrating MEV-Boost's intended design could not supply that missing element.

The court also distinguished precedents involving spoofing, where orders create a misleading impression before being canceled. Here, the lure transactions executed and also were not placed on a regulated market with rules prohibiting the conduct relied upon in those precedents.

That reasoning does not establish a universal requirement that wire fraud occur on a regulated market, nor does it determine whether all forms of MEV extraction are lawful.

Recent findings suggest that in a March 30 letter, the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association (SIFMA) argued that exposing pending trades to sandwiching and front-running can conflict with securities-market expectations. It called for technical protections or fair-sequencing rules when automated market makers handle securities.

An automated market maker (AMM) lets participants trade against assets committed to a pool using software-defined pricing. The ordering of those trades can affect who receives a favorable price and who captures the resulting profit.

Keeping an investor's pending instruction private and deciding who processes it first are economically significant choices.

Recent findings suggest that the SEC's Sept. 17 order created temporary, conditional relief from the definition of an exchange for qualifying tokenized National Market System stock venues using permissioned AMM pools. Certain liquidity providers trading proprietary capital received separate relief from the dealer definition until Sept. 17, 2031.

According to recent reports, the order retains applicable securities antifraud and antimanipulation provisions, including Exchange Act Section 10(b) and Rule 10b-5. Its conditions include permissioned access, public notices, records, and specified trading stoppages.

A venue must describe policies and procedures designed to address it, or state that it has none. It must disclose known material risks, explain any mitigation and compensation arrangements, and describe trading-abuse monitoring or acknowledge its absence.

A venue's published account of its protections can be detailed while leaving investors exposed to risks the operator expressly acknowledges.

Sources indicate that the SEC's public list, reviewed Nov. 16, contains four notice filers. Their submission dates range from TSV LLC's Sept. 23 notice to Formation Securities' Nov. 9 filing.

TSV LLC's current notice says Canton's architecture generally avoids broadcasting readable pending transaction contents to unrelated participants, aiming to reduce opportunities for conventional public-mempool front-running and sandwich attacks.

The operator still acknowledges risks of information leakage, sequencing, compromised infrastructure, and collusion.

According to recent reports, OKXICE's Nov. 5 notice disclosed that it has no policies and procedures designed to address MEV. That sits alongside general protections, including permissioned participation, participant minimum-output settings, surveillance and the ability to revoke access for manipulative trading. OKXICE says those features mitigate, rather than eliminate, MEV risk.

Its planned pools use Uniswap v4 on XLayer, where the notice claims the sequencer generally orders transactions according to offered network fees.

In a recent development, perpetuals.com's notice proposes generally first-in, first-out sequencing, with priority for trading-halt instructions and signed arrival receipts intended to make ordering verifiable. Yet its affiliated sequencer would receive nonpublic transaction information.

A private pending-transaction route can reduce exposure to outsiders while leaving a concentrated information advantage to manage.

Its October notice describes safeguards that were not fully implemented and surveillance intended to precede trading. Formation's notice likewise describes planned safeguards for its Solana venue.

Preventing an abusive trade, detecting it afterward, and compensating its victim are different functions.

TSV indicates participants generally should not expect compensation for market or impermanent losses, compromised participant systems or losses caused by unaffiliated third parties, unless it expressly agrees otherwise or the law requires it.

Recent findings suggest that perpetuals.com reports no established compensation policy for the risks described in its notice. Formation specifically excludes compensation for lost or compromised private keys or wallets, which does not establish a general recovery guarantee for other losses.

Criminal proof, securities-venue duties and compensation terms address different parts of investor protection.

A disclosed safeguard is not a guarantee of prevention or repayment.

The acquittal concerns this prosecution. Venue notices include prepares and operator statements, not independently tested controls. Compensation depends on the particular loss, applicable law and agreements; the graphic predicts no liability outcome.

Industry observers note that qualitative mapping of the court's material-misrepresentation finding, the SEC's MEV disclosure and preserved-law provisions, and disclosed venue compensation limits. Branches show distinct questions, not sequence or money flows.

The acquittal concerns this prosecution. Venue notices include looks and operator statements, not independently tested controls. Compensation depends on the particular loss, applicable law and agreements; the graphic predicts no liability outcome.

Recent findings suggest that the SEC order recognizes that sequencing can support price-stabilizing activity as well as abuse. TSV says it does not intend to prevent lawful ordinary post-execution arbitrage or price alignment that avoids misuse of confidential information and other prohibited conduct.

Industry observers note that the dividing line cannot simply be whether someone profits after another trade. Relevant distinctions include whether pending information was misused, how the venue controls ordering, what conduct it addresses, and which legal obligations apply.

For institutions considering these markets, the notices expose concrete choices about privacy, sequencing, surveillance and loss allocation. The execution model determines that a private route still needs controls over privileged information, while a public route needs a response to abusive ordering.

Industry observers note that the next disputed on-chain securities trade would raise questions about what representations were made, what rules applied, who controlled the information and ordering, and what recourse the investor had. Bringing stocks onto a blockchain makes those choices visible.

It has been revealed that U.S. spot XRP ETFs recorded net outflows of $19.1 million between Nov. 9 and Nov. 13, according to SoSoValue.

Ripple-backed Evernorth filed its first quarterly report with the SEC on Nov. 13, ahead of its Nasdaq listing under the ticker XRPN. As of Sept. 30, the tech giant had written down its XRP holdings by $505 million, or almost 60%.

The market value of the 473 million XRP held by the company stood at $516 million on that date, and Evernorth plans to use the reserves for yield strategies and ecosystem development.

Latest Update: Energica rises from the ashes with intends for cheaper electric motorcycles

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (744 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under latest international ownership.
  • Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.
  • Energica notes motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Italian electric motorcycle maker, which ceased operations in 2024 after entering judicial liquidation, has announced a major revival under latest international ownership. And while the Energica name is returning, the company behind it is going to look quite different this time around.

Perhaps the biggest change is where the motorcycles will actually be built.

Energica notes motorcycle production is moving to Asia, while design, engineering, research and development, as well as responsibility for technical and quality standards, will remain in Italy. The new manufacturing setup is expected to significantly reduce production costs, allowing Energica to cut motorcycle prices by around 20% compared to its previous models.

That could be a big deal for a organization whose motorcycles were widely praised for their performance and technology, but were also firmly positioned at the premium end of the market.

In a recent development, the revival comes after Energica was acquired by Energica Pte. Ltd., a Singapore-based firm backed by international private investors. Importantly, much of the technological know-how isn’t disappearing overseas with the manufacturing. Energica indicates its core engineering and design leadership remains in Italy, including longtime CTO Giampiero Testoni and designer Paolo Imeni.

The first motorcycle to make its comeback will be the Energica Experia, the organization’s adventure-oriented electric sport-tourer. After that, Energica plans to progressively restart production of the Ego, Eva Ribelle, and EsseEsse9, eventually bringing its entire previous lineup back to market.

According to recent reports, at least initially, those motorcycles will use their existing platforms, which should help Energica get bikes rolling off the production line faster without having to develop and homologate entirely upcoming machines. But upgrades are already planned, including a new battery and improvements to range, efficiency, performance, and reliability.

Energica is also specifically targeting Europe, the United States, and Australia as it rebuilds its dealer and service networks. Existing owners haven’t been forgotten either. The organization states service has already resumed and spare-parts shipments have restarted to dealers in several countries.

For anyone who followed the electric motorcycle industry over the last decade, Energica’s disappearance was a particularly painful one. This wasn’t some startup with a couple of renderings and a dream. Energica built some of the highest-performance electric motorcycles on the road and spent four seasons supplying the motorcycles for the FIM MotoE World Cup, experience that helped develop its high-voltage and DC fast-charging technology.

Now the company gets something relatively rare in the motorcycle industry: a second chance.

And if moving production to Asia really can knock around 20% off Energica’s prices while retaining the Italian engineering that made the bikes special in the first place, Energica 2.0 might have a considerably better shot at turning great electric motorcycles into a sustainable business.

Industry observers note that it seems like moving toward Asian manufacturing is all but inevitable here. It was the expensive European manufacturing of low-volume motorcycles that weighed so heavily on Energica’s balance sheets in the years up to their financial troubles, and so shifting production to countries with both the expertise and the cost benefits for motorcycle manufacturing simply makes sense.

In a recent development, energica isn’t alone in discovering the economics of moving electric motorcycle production to Asia. Zero Motorcycles spent years manufacturing its bikes in California before beginning a major shift toward production in the Philippines in 2023, including both complete motorcycles and major subassemblies. Now the tech giant works with multiple factories, including major manufacturers like Zongshen in China, to reduce production costs for its electric motorcycles while still maintaining the ‘designed in California’ marketing angle.

It’s too early to tell how the newly introduced strategy will play out for Energica, but the fact that the firm is now following a more well-worn trail is a positive sign for those who have spent the last two years hoping for a revival.

#18096. Tesla to end Cybertruck production as sales stall at ~10% of plan

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1014 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla to end Cybertruck production as sales stall at ~10% of plan

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla is ending Cybertruck production.
  • Industry observers note that musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production.
  • Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla is ending Cybertruck production. CEO Elon Musk confirmed early Friday that the automaker will “wind down” the electric pickup at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027, about three and a half years after the first deliveries.

Industry observers note that musk says it’s to make room for more Cybercab production. But Giga Texas isn’t short on space. The Cybertruck is short on buyers, and it sells at roughly a tenth of the 250,000 units a year Tesla built its line for.

Tesla will be winding down production of the Cybertruck at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of next year to make room for increased Cybercab production.

In a recent development, that’s all he said. Nothing yet on how long Tesla will keep selling inventory or what happens to parts and service for existing owners.

Tesla doesn’t break out Cybertruck deliveries. It lumps them into “Other Models,” along with the Model S, Model X, and now the Semi.

That bucket tells the story anyway. Tesla delivered 8,295 “Other Models” in Q3 2026, down 48% year-over-year and the lowest since Q2 2021. With Model S and Model X production over since April, we estimated that 7,000 to 8,000 of those were Cybertrucks.

Recent findings suggest that that’s a pace of about 30,000 trucks a year. Tesla planned the Cybertruck line for 250,000 units annually, and its latest shareholder letter still lists more than 125,000 units of installed capacity. So the truck is selling at about 12% of plan, and roughly a quarter of what’s actually installed.

Sources indicate that the US numbers from Cox Automotive are worse. Cox estimates 3,519 Cybertruck sales in Q1 2026 and 3,744 in Q2, down from 14,416 in Q3 2024.

Recent findings suggest that and not all of those were real customers. S&P Global Mobility data indicated SpaceX bought 1,279 Cybertrucks in Q4 2025, and Musk’s companies took 1,339 in total, about 19% of US registrations that quarter. If it wasn’t for Musk’s self-dealing, the Cybertruck would probably be dead already.

Tesla tried to fix demand. It introduced a cheaper rear-wheel-drive version in 2025 and pulled it months later, then brought a cheaper dual-motor trim to customers this summer. And then it raised prices by $5,000 in August. The dual-motor now starts at $74,990.

The “make room” explanation doesn’t hold up. Giga Texas has more than 10 million square feet of factory floor, by Tesla’s own count, and the Cybertruck line is already running at about a quarter of its installed capacity. Most of it is sitting idle.

According to recent reports, the Cybercab also isn’t at a volume where it’s fighting anyone for floor space. Texas had 463 Cybercabs registered as of late October, and Tesla built a separate line for its “unboxed” manufacturing process.

If Tesla needs more Cybercab capacity down the road, it has the space. What it doesn’t want is to keep paying for a truck with its own stainless steel body, its own castings, and its own supply chain at 30,000 units a year.

Let’s call this what it is. Tesla isn’t ending the Cybertruck because the Cybercab needs room. It’s ending it because nobody’s buying it at anything close to the volume Tesla planned, and supporting a low-volume vehicle this unique is expensive.

Recent findings suggest that I wouldn’t be surprised if Tesla lost a couple of billions on the Cybertruck experiment. Between R&D, pushing suppliers to produce 250,000 trucks per year, and deploying its own production line capable of 125,000 trucks per year, Tesla has invested billions. And with only ~70,000 trucks delivered in roughly 3 years, it probably never made any positive cash flow from the program.

Sources indicate that they are just in-between growth phases. No need to panic just because they have discontinued three vehicles and the last successful vehicle they released was the Model Y in early 2020.

The Cybercab line gives Musk a forward-looking reason to wrap a product failure in. Tesla did the same thing when it ended Model S and Model X production this year to free up Fremont for Optimus. It’s a lot easier to say “we need room for the future” than “this didn’t sell.”.

We’ve remarked it many times: the Cybertruck is genuinely impressive to drive. Steer-by-wire and rear-wheel steering are real engineering, and nobody else has put them in a production pickup. But Tesla built a 250,000-unit factory for a polarizing $75,000+ truck that can’t be sold in Europe or most right-hand-drive markets. It just cancelled it for Australia and New Zealand two weeks ago. The math was never going to work.

It’s truly a sign of Tesla today. Musk used to talk about having a more traditional electric truck design if Cybertruck fails, but I doubt we will see that. Again, Elon is betting the house on autonomy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home » Trendsetter News » Stellar Floats XLM Rewards Pool After 1,000% Payments Jump.

Stellar is exploring an XLM rewards pool funded by network fees as monthly payment volume rises tenfold.

Stellar is considering a proposal to reward XLM holders who lock tokens and contribute utility to the network. Crypto market commentator All In Crypto highlights the idea in a video reviewing Stellar’s third-quarter webinar, asking whether rising network activity can translate into stronger demand for XLM.

The proposal would put network-generated fees into an XLM rewards pool. But Dixon, speaking during the webinar, stresses that it remains an early concept open to feedback, not an approved change or a promised payout.

“I’m not sure this is the right proposal,” she says, urging participants to read the accompanying paper and explore its interactive dashboard before commenting. Her central argument is that “utility should drive XLM.”.

The webinar reports that monthly payment volume on Stellar rose from roughly $1.8 billion in January to $18.5 billion in October. October’s figure was 89% higher than September’s, following eight consecutive months of growth.

It has been revealed that another $7.5 billion reportedly moved during November’s first 10 days. Those figures describe money moving across the network, however, not purchases of XLM or returns accruing to token holders.

Industry observers note that all In Crypto is openly bullish but acknowledges uncertainty over the token’s future value. That distinction matters: greater use of Stellar’s infrastructure does not, by itself, establish how much additional XLM users need to hold.

The webinar also describes a U.S. Bank pilot in which the bank issued a dollar-backed stablecoin called USBDC and used it to settle a cross-border payment between its North American and European entities. According to the presentation, minting, redemption, freezing and claw-back controls operated at the protocol level, without custom contract logic.

Industry observers note that stellar’s Project Throughput offers another glimpse of its ambitions. The webinar cites early benchmarks of roughly 1.2 million payments per second on one machine and about seven million across eight machines.

Those are technology-preview results, not reported production-network throughput. The project is available on Futurenet with open-source code for developers to test.

Now, the unresolved question is less whether Stellar can process more activity than how that activity benefits XLM.

The rewards proposal could create another connection between network use and token ownership, but its design, eligibility requirements and eventual adoption remain unsettled.

Hackers found a way to steal crypto without hacking wallets, and Ledger was caught in the attack

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cryptoslate

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ledger's website was among 178 organizations exposed to malicious scripts that could redirect cryptocurrency payments to hackers, researchers reported Monday.
  • Cybersecurity firm Report URI discovered the malware in 188 website scripts associated with major brands, including Ledger, BBC, CNN, Zoom, Salesforce and HSBC.
  • The firm examined 1,611 scripts delivered through Optimizely, a platform businesses use to test and personalize their websites.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ledger's website was among 178 organizations exposed to malicious scripts that could redirect cryptocurrency payments to hackers, researchers reported Monday.

Cybersecurity firm Report URI discovered the malware in 188 website scripts associated with major brands, including Ledger, BBC, CNN, Zoom, Salesforce and HSBC.

The firm examined 1,611 scripts delivered through Optimizely, a platform businesses use to test and personalize their websites. Attackers had inserted malicious instructions into customer-specific JavaScript, allowing infected code to reach visitors through a service those websites already trusted.

The attack exposed a vulnerability for cryptocurrency users: hackers could redirect funds without stealing private keys or compromising wallets.

Ledger's inclusion in the affected websites does not establish that its hardware wallets, firmware, or signing infrastructure were breached.

The malicious code was designed to identify crypto addresses displayed on websites and replace them with destinations controlled by attackers.

According to recent reports, researchers at Hudson Rock found that the malware could alter wallet addresses in visible text, input fields, links, and clipboard operations. It supported multiple blockchain networks, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Tron, and Litecoin.

For example, a user copying a legitimate Bitcoin payment address from an infected page could unknowingly paste an attacker-controlled address into their wallet application.

If the user then approved the transaction without verifying the destination, the funds would go to the attacker.

The technique circumvents an important layer of cryptocurrency security because the wallet can function exactly as intended while authorizing a payment to the wrong recipient.

Hudson Rock found no evidence that the recovered malware directly extracted wallet seed phrases or initiated unauthorized blockchain transactions through wallet-signing functions.

Researchers described code that could alter a displayed or copied crypto address before a transfer, without needing the private key.

According to recent reports, illustrative flow: the remote payload reaches the page. The recovered snippet also contains a fallback.

Illustrative flow for embedded-fallback variants: a host block may stop the fetch while local code remains available, subject to browser policy.

Destination substitution can divert a user-authorized payment without the malware signing it.

According to recent reports, presence of poisoned code does not prove execution or a completed transfer. The fallback concerns two recovered variants and remains subject to browser policy. No seed extraction or wallet-signing calls were identified in the recovered samples; this is not a blanket security assurance.

Qualitative reconstruction of researcher-described code paths. The panel compares illustrative remote-request outcomes for the embedded-fallback variants, not observed victim sessions. No quantitative geometry or fresh calculation.

Presence of poisoned code does not prove execution or a completed transfer. The fallback concerns two recovered variants and remains subject to browser policy. No seed extraction or wallet-signing calls were identified in the recovered samples; this is not a blanket security assurance.

However, the attack appears to have generated financial proceeds.

Report URI identified approximately $7,040 received by attacker-linked crypto addresses as of 19:25 UTC on Nov. 16. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $5,380, while additional transactions involved Litecoin, Tron, Ethereum, and BNB Smart Chain.

Researchers also identified code associated with the Coruna and DarkSword iPhone exploit kits, potentially exposing visitors using vulnerable Apple devices to additional attacks.

These capabilities expanded the threat beyond crypto holders to customers interacting with infected websites.

Report URI stated a large-scale cleanup reduced the number of infected scripts in its sample from 169 at 20:56 UTC to just one at 21:52 UTC on Nov. 16. Ledger's affected script was reportedly cleaned at approximately 20:41 UTC.

However, the researchers also discovered embedded copies of the malicious code, meaning blocking the attackers' remote servers alone might not eliminate every infection.

The central mystery is how the attackers got permission to modify scripts for so many unrelated organizations.

The researchers have not established whether the intrusion originated from compromised credentials, an Optimizely system, or another access route.

At publication, the investigation had not established the number of affected visitors or the full extent of financial losses, leaving the attackers' initial access method and the campaign's ultimate impact unresolved.

Recent findings suggest that bet25 is changing this with the Zero Margin Sportsbook, setting the new rules of sports betting. Built on honesty, clear numbers, and fair pricing, Bet25 removes traditional bookmaker tricks, so the real payout is received.

In a standard sportsbook, the odds you see are not the true odds. The bookmaker trims 5% to 10% off the price of each game to guarantee their own cut before you even place a bet.

On a single match, this might look small. But on combo bets, it becomes a serious problem. Because combo odds multiply together, the hidden house cuts multiply too. Every leg you add gives you a payout that is much lower than the actual math says it should be.

The Bet25 Zero Margin Sportsbook is not a temporary promo or a short-lived boost. It is a completely different way to run a sportsbook:.

In a recent development, A normal bookmaker takes a cut on pick 1, pick 2, pick 3, and so on. Bet25 charges one single 5% fee whether you pick one game or five.

The difference is easy to see on a multi-leg ticket. Take a simple 5-leg combo where each pick has a true 50/50 probability. A regular bookmaker will usually offer around 1.87 on each outcome to keep their cut, but a zero-margin sportsbook will price it at 2.0, again because of no hidden margin inside.

Same five picks. Same $100 bet. Exactly the same risk. But Bet25 pays out $755 more because no hidden cuts were multiplied along the way.

Almost every betting site claims to have “the best odds.” Bet25 doesn’t need hype or marketing talk. Instead, the advice is simple: just compare.

Open a betting site side by side with the Bet25 Zero Margin Sportsbook. Check any match, build a 3-leg or 4-leg combo on both, and look at the final payouts. You will see the difference right away. It is not marketing – it is pure math.

#18089. Latest Update: BYD’s electric hypercar hits 312 mph, first production car over 500 km/h

📅 06 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1053 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: BYD’s electric hypercar hits 312 mph, first production car over 500 km/h

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1053 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h.
  • The FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run.
  • BYD declared the record on X this morning, saying the U9 Xtreme “has done the impossible” and calling it “the fastest production car on the planet.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

BYD’s Yangwang U9 Xtreme just reached 503.17 km/h (312.66 mph) on a closed highway in Abu Dhabi, making it the first production car ever to go faster than 500 km/h.

The FIA and Guinness World Records both recognized the run. It’s the all-electric hypercar’s second top-speed record in just over a year, and the one it broke was its own.

BYD declared the record on X this morning, saying the U9 Xtreme “has done the impossible” and calling it “the fastest production car on the planet.”.

Abu Dhabi closed a 10 km section of the Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed International Road (E11), in the emirate’s Al Dhafra Region, for the attempt. That gave the team a 7 km straight. Marc Basseng, the German racing driver who set the car’s previous record, was behind the wheel again.

Industry observers note that it took two days. Basseng maxed out at 490 km/h on the first day, per the FIA. After an overnight round of changes to the rear wing, damping, and tire pressures, he got to 503.17 km/h on his second attempt of November 1.

The previous mark was 496.22 km/h (308 mph), set at Germany’s ATP Papenburg proving ground in September 2025. That run had already pushed the Bugatti Chiron Super Sport 300+ and its 490.48 km/h from 2019 off the top of the list.

In a recent development, and it comes just days after BYD released footage of a U9 Xtreme crashing into a guardrail at about 280 mph during an earlier high-speed test. The driver walked away unharmed. BYD went right back out and hit 457.89 km/h on the next run.

According to recent reports, the U9 Xtreme is the track-focused version of the Yangwang U9, the flagship supercar from BYD’s luxury brand. It uses four electric motors, each rated at 555 kW and spinning up to 30,000 rpm, for 2,220 kW combined. That’s over 3,000 PS, or nearly 3,000 hp.

It runs on a 1,200-volt architecture with a track-grade version of BYD’s Blade Battery. Those are LFP cells, the same chemistry BYD puts in its cheapest city cars.

Sources indicate that for context, the Rimac Nevera R, which snagged a pile of EV world records last year, tops out at 431.45 km/h. The U9 Xtreme also holds the production EV lap record at the Nürburgring Nordschleife at 6:59.157.

In a recent development, only 30 will be built, and BYD is charging around $3 million apiece. Don’t expect to see one in the US, where BYD doesn’t sell passenger cars.

In a recent development, the biggest one: this is a single-direction run. The two Guinness titles listed for the attempt, highest speed by a production car and by an electric production car, are both specified as “single direction.” BYD’s post claims four Guinness records, but the FIA’s announcement only lists those two for this run.

Industry observers note that production car top speed records have traditionally been the average of two runs in opposite directions, within an hour, to cancel out wind and road grade. That’s how Koenigsegg got its 447.19 km/h record with the Agera RS in 2017.

It has been revealed that bugatti took heat for exactly this in 2019, when the Chiron hit 490 km/h one way on a pre-production car. Bugatti itself said it wasn’t an official record.

The car also ran on bespoke semi-slick tires developed with Giti Tire. It’s not clear whether the 30 customer cars will get them.

In a recent development, A Chinese automaker best known for $10,000 city cars now builds the fastest production car in the world, and it’s electric. Not long ago, the conventional wisdom was that EVs couldn’t sustain high top speeds because the battery and motors would overheat long before the car ran out of road. BYD just ran 503 km/h on LFP cells. LFP cells!

It has been revealed that but we’d hold BYD to the same standard we held Bugatti to. A one-way run on a highway with a 7 km straight is a great demo, not a definitive record, but impressive nonetheless.

It has been revealed that roadster 2 will now never be a record holder. It simple can't compete with today's hypercars nevermind those in 2028 when we actually see one leave a factory. Although with Tesla's record, it's usually 4 years from demo to production so that makes it 2030 for the Roadster 2.

And either way, let’s be honest: this is about marketing. Nobody is going to drive one of these 30 cars at 500 km/h. But it works. It’s a halo for Yangwang ahead of its new ultra-luxury sedan and for BYD’s push into Europe, and it makes the “Chinese cars are cheap copies” crowd look out of date.

Meanwhile, Tesla promised a Roadster that would hit over 250 mph back in 2017. Nine years later, it’s still not in production.

According to recent reports, the real question now is whether Bugatti or Koenigsegg answers with a two-way 500 km/h run. Koenigsegg states its Jesko Absolut can theoretically do it, but it has never attempted a run. Is BYD what finally makes them try?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth has suffered substantial losses on its XRP ventures amid the persistent volatility facing the broad crypto market since the third quarter of 2026.
  • According to recent reports, the firm has reported a massive write-down of its XRP holdings for Q3 2026 in a recent filing with the U.S.
  • On Tuesday, November 17, Evernorth reported a substantial decline in the value of its XRP holdings after the firm wrote down over $505 million in its latest financial filing with the SEC.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth has suffered substantial losses on its XRP ventures amid the persistent volatility facing the broad crypto market since the third quarter of 2026.

According to recent reports, the firm has reported a massive write-down of its XRP holdings for Q3 2026 in a recent filing with the U.S. SEC, drawing attention from the broader crypto community.

On Tuesday, November 17, Evernorth reported a substantial decline in the value of its XRP holdings after the firm wrote down over $505 million in its latest financial filing with the SEC.

Notably, Evernorth issued a Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, disclosing that it holds around 346 million XRP, now valued at about $342 million.

This has drawn attention across the XRP community and sparked discussions about the growing impact of persistent volatility on investors’ funds, as Evernorth’s XRP report marks a sharp drop from its initial valuation of $847 million.

Apparently, the firm reported that the tokens are now valued at about 40 cents per dollar of their initial worth. This means that the leading XRP treasury firm has reduced the value of its XRP holdings by nearly 60%.

Sources indicate that it is vital to note that the massive drop in the value of Evernorth’s XRP holdings does not mean that the firm has sold off its XRP. Rather, it marks a write-down in its previously listed XRP value.

The move may have been influenced by the persistent market drawdown, especially after XRP lost support at the key $1 level, closing steadily around $0.90 over the past few days.

Furthermore, Evernorth has specified that it has no intention of reversing the write-downs, even if the price of XRP later recovers.
